First of all, I would like to point out that I am a truck driver, a retired wagoner, having spent about 10 years driving passenger cars and municipal buses and 25 years on the road as a heavy wagoner, having traveled and known almost all of Brazil and I can say with all certainty that this game is almost perfect both in structure and logistics as well as operational, as it gives a perfect reality of what the life of the truck driver is like on the roads. Arrows, bifurcations, fines and especially the interactivity between trucks and private cars at roundabouts. There is a lot of attention to be paid (to double the attention) because that is really what happens. The game is great, both in graphics, logistics, gameplay and especially for the beauty of the roads and why not say the maneuvering work of the horses in the deliveries. I give myself the right to give a tip to you who are starting. Never maneuver a truck through the right mirror. Every carter, (you can see) he opens the door on the left, puts a foot on the door step, accelerates the truck a little and maneuvers looking at the whole terrain. Never trust the (come, come, go) because if he misses and you damage the load and do not warn you it is the driver who pays the loss. (You know what he says? The driver is you)

I still can't explain why driving a truck for hours is so much fun, but here we are.

Seriously, I can spend all day doing actual work, come home, turn on my PC, and voluntarily start another job. Only this time I'm delivering furniture to Germany and getting annoyed at someone cutting me off on the motorway.

And I absolutely love it.

There's just something about ETS2. Pick a delivery, get on the road, put some music on, and drive. Sometimes I don't even care about the money or growing my company. I just want to drive somewhere.

The trucks feel great, there's a ridiculous amount of stuff to explore, and SCS has kept this thing alive for so long that it's honestly impressive. You can always find another route, another truck to try, or another excuse to spend an evening doing absolutely nothing exciting.

Of course, the traffic AI still has moments where you wonder if the other drivers are actively trying to commit insurance fraud. And yes, there's quite a bit of DLC. But after all the enjoyment I've gotten out of this game, I'm really not going to complain too much.

It's not a game I'd recommend to absolutely everyone. If you need constant action, you'll probably be bored within fifteen minutes.

But for me? It's one of those games I can always come back to. No pressure, no competition, no nonsense. Just another delivery.

And probably another speeding fine.

Recommended. Easily.

This is a pretty good game if you're looking for something relaxing and you like driving trucks.
- The graphics are pretty nice.
- The trucks are all pretty accurate to real life and have lots of stuff to customize.
- There's a variety of cargo for you to deliver.
- You can start and build up your own company, hire drivers, and build a trucking empire.
- The devs are still releasing updates and DLCs for the game despite it being several years old.
- There's a pretty large and active modding community for this game, so if there's something you feel the game is missing chances are someone has made a mod for it.

Nominated for the 2025 Labor of Love award.

A relaxing and satisfying gaming experience awaits you in Euro Truck Simulator 2. The game offers a unique and engaging gaming experience that allows you to drive your own truck across Europe, deliver cargo and build your own transport company.

One of the most enjoyable aspects of the game is the driving itself. The game's driving physics and behaviour are incredibly realistic, making every bend and hill feel like a real challenge. It's easy to get lost in the beauty of the virtual landscape as you drive through picturesque towns and countryside.

As you progress through the game, you can upgrade your truck and customise it to your liking. You can also hire drivers and expand your business, giving you a sense of ownership and success as you build your own truck empire.

The game also features a great community of players who are always happy to help or give advice. Whether joining a convoy or just chatting with other players online, the game creates a sense of camaraderie among players.

Overall, Euro Truck Simulator 2 offers a positive gaming experience that is both relaxing and challenging. The game offers a sense of freedom and exploration that is rarely found in other games, and it is easy to get lost in the many hours of fun it offers.

Basic Driving Controls

W, A, S, D – Accelerate, Brake/Reverse, Steer Left, Steer Right
Space – Handbrake
E – Start/Stop Engine
R – Change Radio Station
Q / E – Left / Right Turn Signals
H – Horn
L – Headlights (Press multiple times for different modes)
F – Hazard Lights
P – Wipers (Toggle through different speeds)
B – Retarder (Slows the truck without braking)

Camera & Navigation

C – Cruise Control Toggle
M – Open Map
TAB – Open Multiplayer Player List (If using TruckersMP)
1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 – Different Camera Views
Mouse Scroll – Zoom in/out when using interior view
F5 – Cycle GPS Zoom Levels
F6 – Show Job Details
F7 – Roadside Assistance & Tow Service
F8 – View Messages (Such as fines or job warnings)
Enter – Confirm Selection (Used for refueling, repairs, or picking up/dropping off cargo)

Surprisingly fun and addictive game. Once you build up your character's attributes you can make bank. Some of the deliveries can be 1,000+ km/miles. Just turn on the radio or listen to your own manually added tunes and enjoy the ride. You can purchase multiple trucking locations and hire drivers for each of them who in turn make money for you as they complete deliveries.

There are a good number of truck manufacturers to choose from and plenty of options and upgrades, not to include DLC which further enhances upgrades. This game has quite a bit of replay value and much of that comes from the devs who continually provide updates and the modding community who tirelessly provide worthwhile mods. Get busy and start building your trucking empire!

2369 hours so far. And this is only after I bought it via steam, not including the countless hours before that. This is my go-to relaxation tool after a heavy day in the office. The base game is already quite large - grab yourself ProMods and you got most of Europe to rumble through. The game has extremely wide modding community - you want to drive a bus? Here is a bus. You want to drive a car - here is a car. Not happy with the default traffic - here is hundreds of new traffic models. You want realistic economy and real gas prices? There are mods for that as well. Realistic day/night cycle? Sure! (though it is quite depressing during the winter). You don't like the original graphics? There is mod for that as well. You can even put SweetFX on top of that. The physics was improved quite a lot lately (thank you SCS! ), and you can change some things on-the-fly. Did I mention that I can see the building that I live in inside the game?
Anyways, just go buy the game - I need to go finish my delivery from Sicily to Sweden. With the new MAN.

Euro Truck Simulator 2 is a great way to unwind — throw on some music, hit the road, and just enjoy the drive. In VR, especially on the Quest 3, the experience really comes alive. Turning your head to check mirrors or admire the scenery makes it feel that much more immersive.
